en: What foreign force has taken from us
We shall take back with the sabre.
From the Italian land to Poland,
We shall unite with the nation.
Bonaparte has given us the example
Of how we are to win.
We shall return across the sea.
Now there a father to his Basia
notes: line 1.2: 'Kiedy' here means 'while, as long as' (not 'when'); Wybicki's 1797 manuscript has 'Póki' with the same sense. This is the official text of 1927, which differs from the 1797 original in wording and stanzas.
line 1.4: 'Szablą' — the sabre, the szabla of the Polish cavalry.
line 2.1: Jan Henryk Dąbrowski, commander of the Polish Legions in Italy (1797), for whom the song was written; 'Ref:' is the text's label and kept.
line 2.3: 'za twoim przewodem', under (following) your lead or command.
line 5.1-5.2: Stefan Czarniecki, who fought the Swedes after their invasion of 1655 (the Deluge); 'zabór' is the Swedish seizure (occupation) of the country. Poznań is a city.
line 5.4: 'Wrócim się przez morze' — 'we shall return across the sea', the Legions' way home from Italy; it also echoes Czarniecki's crossing to Als in 1658 (not said in the text).
line 7.1: Basia, a pet form of Barbara, the father's daughter.
line 7.3: 'jeno' (only, just) and 'pono' (it seems, they say) are archaic.
line 7.4: 'tarabany', drums or kettledrums (an old loanword).
